Each release note is carried by Codex behavior: 4.9.2 landed migrations (landing.mjs + lifecycle deliver, landing.test), 4.9.3/4.10.1 spec decisions without section approvals (discovery.md, skills.test), 4.10.0 build here (lifecycle here, execution.md, offer/skills tests), 4.10.2 agent handoff refusals and descriptions (offer.mjs, agent-ready, offer.test); 4.11.0 benchmark excluded as Claude-only, with the runtime reason and the Codex adaptation notes in README's Codex adaptation boundaries.

parseWalkReadiness/landedMigrations live in landing.mjs, with destructive detection widened (more DROP forms, UPDATE…SET, ALTER COLUMN…TYPE) and non-.sql migrations (Alembic, Knex, Rails, Django) judged by their forward half, any drop/alter/rename/execute call treated as destructive; ask/human/no-apply/unchecked-out target noted. ACTIVE_MS and buildingInSession live in offer.mjs; upstream's activeInSession is lastActivity there, over Codex worktree activity (.builder/<feature>/ and .builder/gates/ recursively, tracked ledger.md, Git index, HEAD commit time). sharedBranch is unnecessary by construction: every Codex feature has its own builder/<feature> branch, and start refuses an existing one.

No Claude fleet in Codex. Landing is lifecycle.mjs deliver: after the verified fast-forward/CAS it reads the target's Walk readiness, applies additive migrations under apply_mode agent in the target checkout (logged), and records applied, applied-dirty (files the commands left, so the clean-target checks do not block silently), failed (what ran and what is left) or a note with the exact command in landing.note/nextAction. The fleet pre-flight's in-session refusal has no script enforcement point in Codex: lifecycle.mjs agent-ready computes the refusal and profiles.md requires the coordinator to run it once before a handoff begins. Shared-branch refusal is unnecessary (per-feature builder/<name> branches).

execution.md Build here: coordinator works PLAN task by task itself, test first, one commit per task (manual apps staged), fast gates at phase close, one-line ledger, no workers/reviewers/final review/deep set/walk/sign-off/verify, stops at built with 'built here — not walked'. Codex keeps the feature worktree (never the starting checkout) and requires the skipped floors before any landing.

Landing brings migrations to the dev DB: lifecycle deliver applies additive ones under apply_mode agent in the target checkout, else notes the command; unchecked-out target is noted for when you switch.
Build here is listed in the Codex invocation line ($builder build/resume <feature> --here) and handoff choices; benchmark help row excluded with the benchmark.

Under build: here the plan's go-ahead shows the Phases table, records 'go-ahead: <who date> (here)', commits and proceeds straight into Build here without profile, worker or landing questions; ignored under --agent-walk.

--here flag, build: here manifest key (lifecycle.mjs here, kept by checkpoints), numbered handoff with here before the build, and walk migrations go to the isolated walk DB while the dev DB gets them at landing.
--here records build: here via lifecycle.mjs here, valid only spec..planned (refused after, routes as usual); resume routes here features to the here go-ahead/build, never workers.

No section approvals: unsettled product choices asked as real decisions (why, what it affects, recommendation, alternatives; never approve/change), implementation details recorded '(assumed at spec) YYYY-MM-DD', --auto takes recommendations, one plain closing summary with no question; numbered handoff includes here.
